statements.label: supported
statements.text: Transposable elements occupy roughly three quarters of the Blumeria hordei genome, while its gene count is low relative to other ascomycetes.
statements.evidence: Compared to other ascomycetes, it contains a low number of genes but a high genomic TE content of approximately 75%.
statements.note: The abstract gives both figures directly: a low gene number and about 75% TE content compared with other ascomycetes.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Long-read RNA sequencing showed that TEs and genes are frequently transcribed together into chimeric transcripts.
statements.evidence: Using long-read RNA sequencing, we detected extensive co-transcription of TEs and genes as TE-gene chimeric transcripts.
statements.note: Extensive TE-gene co-transcription detected by long-read RNA sequencing is reported as a result.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The two sequenced isolates, German TUM1 and Australian AUS1, differ in the fraction of their genome made up of transposable elements.
statements.evidence: assemblies of the German Bh isolate TUM1 and the Australian Bh isolate AUS1
statements.note: Both isolates were assembled and annotated, but no comparison of their TE content is reported either way.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Thousands of transcripts and several TE-derived proteins absent from earlier TE protein predictions arise from the intergenic and TE space of the TUM1 genome.
statements.evidence: The intergenic and TE genomic space of Bh TUM1 gives rise to thousands of transcripts and several novel TE-derived proteins that lack from previous TE protein predictions.
statements.note: This is stated as a finding for the TUM1 assembly.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: MITE insertions inside genic regions lower the expression of the genes that carry them.
statements.evidence: A notable proportion of MITEs were found in genic and near-genic regions, underscoring their potential as tools for gene function exploration.
statements.note: Location in genic regions is reported, but no measurement of any effect on gene expression is described.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Genome-wide screening found 51,369 MITEs in Corchorus capsularis and 50,829 in Corchorus olitorius, assigned to 632 and 539 families respectively.
statements.evidence: Genome-wide analysis identified 51,369 and 50,829 MITEs, classified into 632 and 539 families in CC and C. olitorius, respectively.
statements.note: The counts of elements and families for each species are given in the text.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Thirty-eight MIP markers tested on 30 jute accessions worked for genetic diversity analysis and sorted the accessions into five clusters.
statements.evidence: Validation of thirty-eight randomly selected MIP markers across 30 jute accessions demonstrated their efficacy in genetic diversity analysis, grouping the accessions into five distinct clusters.
statements.note: The validation result, including the five clusters, is reported explicitly.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: More MITE-derived microRNAs were recovered from Corchorus capsularis (11,801) than from Corchorus olitorius (10,921).
statements.evidence: Additionally, 11,801 and 10,921 MITE-derived microRNAs were identified in CC and C. olitorius, emphasizing their roles in genetic and epigenetic regulation.
statements.note: Both counts are reported, and the first is the larger of the two.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: ctDNA dropped after treatment in 14 patients, and 12 of those patients reached complete remission.
statements.evidence: A reduction in the ctDNA was observed after treatment in 14 patients, 12 of whom achieved complete remission.
statements.note: Both numbers come straight from the reported results.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Patients whose diagnostic mutation persisted in cfDNA after treatment relapsed within a year.
statements.evidence: In 12 of the 15 patients with complete remission, the mutation attributed to the disease found at diagnosis cleared with treatment.
statements.note: Mutation clearance is reported, but no relapse or follow-up outcome data appear in the abstract.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: CREBBP was mutated more often than any other gene, in 67% of the patients studied.
statements.evidence: CREBBP was the most frequent mutated gene (67 %).
statements.note: The abstract names CREBBP as the most frequently mutated gene and gives the percentage.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: ctDNA measured at diagnosis correlated positively with total metabolic tumor volume on PET (r = 0.51).
statements.evidence: Correlations were found between the ctDNA at diagnosis and total metabolic tumor volume (r = 0.51; p-value = 0.014)
statements.note: The positive correlation coefficient with total metabolic tumor volume is reported.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Community growth fell as carbamazepine concentration rose, yet the composition of the wastewater community stayed largely the same.
statements.evidence: CBZ reduced growth of the community in a concentration-dependent manner. Still, community composition was largely unaffected by CBZ exposure.
statements.note: Both the concentration-dependent growth reduction and the near-absence of compositional change are reported.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Of the 26 resistance genes screened, four clinically relevant ones rose in relative abundance as the carbamazepine dose increased.
statements.evidence: Among the tested 26 ARGs, four clinically relevant ones ( bla CMY , bla OXA-48 , bla CTX-M , dfr A1) increased in relative abundance in a dose-dependent manner
statements.note: The abstract reports four of the 26 tested ARGs increasing dose-dependently.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: erm F was the only resistance gene whose rise in abundance happened independently of mobile genetic elements, consistent with direct selection.
statements.evidence: In contrast, only erm F abundance rose independently of MGEs, suggesting direct selection.
statements.note: The abstract singles out erm F as the one gene increasing independently of mobile genetic elements.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Removing carbamazepine from treated wastewater effluent lowers resistance gene abundance in receiving surface waters.
statements.evidence: Our results highlight the need to consider non-antibiotic pharmaceuticals in AMR surveillance and environmental risk assessment frameworks, as they may shape the environmental resistome beyond antibiotic exposure.
statements.note: The study exposed communities to carbamazepine but never tested removal or any downstream effect of removing it.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Melanoma patients with higher E2F1 expression fared worse, with a hazard ratio of 1.43.
statements.evidence: Individuals with elevated E2F transcription factor 1 expression had a worse prognosis (HR=1.43, p = 0.01).
statements.note: The worse prognosis and its hazard ratio are reported directly.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: E2F1 expression level predicts how melanoma patients respond to immune checkpoint inhibitor treatment.
statements.evidence: The Tumor Immunization Estimation Resource (TIMER) was used to analyze the invasion of immune cells and associated markers of immune cells.
statements.note: Immune cell infiltration was analysed, but the abstract says nothing about response to any immunotherapy.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: E2F1 expression levels separated tumor from normal tissue well, reaching an area under the curve of 0.949.
statements.evidence: Using the expression level of E2F transcription factor 1, a reliable distinction between tumor and normal tissues can be made (Area Under the Curve =0.949).
statements.note: The discriminative performance and its AUC value are reported as a result.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Both E2F1 mRNA levels and its somatic copy number alterations correlated significantly with the recruitment of several immune cell types.
statements.evidence: immune infiltrations analysis showed that the mRNA expression levels and somatic copy number alterations (SCNA) in E2F transcription factor 1 were significantly correlated with recruitment of several immune cells
statements.note: The immune infiltration analysis reports significant correlations for both expression and copy number alterations.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: PIAS1 mRNA was significantly lower in tumor tissue than in normal oral squamous epithelium, including across 60 matched tumor and normal pairs.
statements.evidence: PIAS1 mRNA expression is significantly lower in tumor tissues than in normal oral cavity squamous epithelium, including in a cohort of 60 patient-matched tumor and normal pairs.
statements.note: The direction of the difference and the matched-pair cohort size are both stated.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: In OSCC cell lines PIAS1 held back migration and invasion driven by TGFβ, and doing so depended on its SUMO E3 activity.
statements.evidence: Functional assays using OSCC cell lines demonstrated that PIAS1 acts in a SUMO E3-dependent manner to suppress TGFβ-induced migration and invasion.
statements.note: The functional assays report exactly this SUMO E3-dependent suppression.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The reduced PIAS1 expression in OSCC tumors is caused by hypermethylation of the PIAS1 promoter.
statements.evidence: Analysis across multiple cohorts revealed that PIAS1 mRNA expression is significantly lower in tumor tissues than in normal oral cavity squamous epithelium
statements.note: The lower expression is reported, but nothing in the abstract tests or rules out a methylation cause.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Among the genes altered in PIAS1-depleted cells, 46 overlapped with TCGA-OSCC data and four of those, INHBA among them, tied to a stemness pathway.
statements.evidence: 46 of these differentially altered hits intersected with The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA)-OSCC datasets, where four of these genes, including INHBA, associated with cell stemness-pathway.
statements.note: Both counts and the INHBA stemness link are given in the results.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The run took about 27 hours from plasma separation to report generation and needed only 40 minutes of hands-on work.
statements.evidence: The total turnaround time from plasma separation to report generation was approximately 27 h, requiring only 40 min of total hands-on time.
statements.note: Both the turnaround time and the hands-on time are reported.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Three pathogenic hotspot mutations plus one copy number gain in PIK3CA were found in the patient sample.
statements.evidence: Three pathogenic hotspot mutations-KRAS G12R, TP53 M246I/M246K, and GNA11-and one copy number gain in PIK3CA were identified
statements.note: The abstract lists the three hotspot mutations and the PIK3CA copy number gain as what was identified.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: The healthy volunteer analysed as a control yielded no detectable variants.
statements.evidence: whereas no variants were detected in a healthy volunteer control
statements.note: The negative control result is stated alongside the patient findings.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: The treatment given to the patient was changed on the basis of the variants the assay reported.
statements.evidence: This report demonstrates that fully automated cfDNA-based NGS can achieve clinically meaningful genomic profiling within 27 h in a community hospital.
statements.note: The report covers feasibility and timing only; no treatment decision or patient outcome is described.

statements.label: not_addressed
statements.text: Drugs that inhibit KIF20A are being tested in clinical trials of kidney renal clear cell carcinoma.
statements.evidence: providing solid theoretical and experimental evidence for KIF20A as a potential anti-cancer therapeutic target
statements.note: KIF20A is proposed as a candidate target, but no clinical testing of any inhibitor is mentioned.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Interfering with KIF20A expression cut the proliferation, migration and invasion of kidney renal clear cell carcinoma cells in culture.
statements.evidence: In vitro experiments have confirmed that interfering with KIF20A expression can effectively inhibit the proliferation, migration, and invasion of KIRC cells.
statements.note: The in vitro experiments report inhibition of all three behaviours.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: High KIF20A expression went together with clinical progression, poorer prognosis and activation of classical oncogenic pathways across multiple cancer types.
statements.evidence: its high expression is closely associated with clinical progression, poor prognosis, and activation of classical oncogenic pathways in multiple cancers
statements.note: This set of associations with high expression is reported in the results.

statements.label: supported
statements.text: Tumor growth in nude mice was reduced when KIF20A was knocked down.
statements.evidence: in vivo experimental results indicate that interfering with KIF20A can inhibit tumor growth in nude mice
statements.note: The in vivo experiment reports inhibited tumor growth in nude mice.
